verdict.rationale: Bevy itself ships as an official Rust crate: it is added as a normal dependency, resolves on crates.io (0.19.1), and has in-depth reference documentation, so a developer or agent can build directly against first-party code. The SDK is only offered for Rust and is pre-1.0, with breaking changes in each release. Community users confirm they had to deal with regular breaking changes, which hurts agents trained on older APIs. Missing for 10: official SDKs for languages beyond Rust, a stable 1.0 API surface, agent-oriented SDK docs (no llms.txt or markdown docs), and independent hands-on corroboration of building against the SDK.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can build against official SDKs

citations.quote: Bevy is just a normal Rust dependency. You can either add it to an existing Rust project or create a new one.
Pre-1.0 with breaking changes each release — a real caveat for agents trained on older APIs.
Learn how to use Bevy's types, traits and methods using the in-depth reference documentation, complete with inline examples.
unless you're willing to get your hands dirty and deal with regular breaking changes, I don't yet recommend staking your livelihood on it.
